name: Contracts
description: Agreements, parties, clauses, obligations, payment terms, renewal, termination and governing law.
purpose: Turn contracts and amendments into a queryable graph of who owes what to whom, when, and under which law, so obligations and key dates can be tracked across a contract portfolio.
scope: In scope: agreement metadata, parties and signatories, clause types, obligations, payment terms, contract term and renewal, termination conditions and governing law. Out of scope: negotiation history, redlines, and legal interpretation or risk scoring of clause wording.
stories: As a contract manager I want to see every agreement's expiry date and auto-renewal flag so that I can act before notice deadlines pass.
As a finance analyst I want each payment term linked to its payer, payee, amount and currency so that I can reconcile contracted fees against invoices.
As in-house counsel I want obligations linked to the clause and party they come from so that I can check which commitments our company owes and to whom.
cqs: Which parties are bound by each agreement?
Who signed each agreement, on behalf of which party, and on what date?
Which agreements expire before a given date and which of them renew automatically?
What obligations does a given party owe, to whom, and under which clause?
What payment amounts, currencies and due periods apply to each agreement, and who pays whom?
Under which conditions can each agreement be terminated, and how many days of notice are required?
Which jurisdiction's law governs each agreement?
Which amendments modify a given agreement?
Which agreements contain a confidentiality or limitation-of-liability clause?
